Each maximal-point cone retracts linearly and S_n-equivariantly onto its base Delta_T, leaving a simplex (r<=k) or the (k-1)-skeleton of the (n-1)-simplex. A standard acyclic matching gives choose(n-1,k) spheres dimension k-1. The integral augmented boundary kernel is wedge^k ker(sum:Z^n to Z), yielding the determinant cycle-character formula. All maximal original nerve facets have dimension k but lower (k-1) homology is nonzero, so not Cohen–Macaulay. Literal intersection and rank checks for small n corroborate but do not prove universality.
